meta.titre: Information Systems at Work: components, types and the managers they serve
meta.sous_theme: Components and types of information system

sections.contenu_markdown: At a supermarket in Yaounde the till records every sale as it happens. At the end of the month the manager reads a report that shows which goods sell best, and the owner uses a forecast to decide whether to open a second shop. These are three different information systems working on related data. Examination questions ask you to name the parts of an information system, to match a type of system to a situation, and to explain how an organisation benefits.

items: Data are raw facts and figures; information is data processed into a form that is useful for a decision.
An organisation has operational staff who do the daily work, middle managers who control it, and senior managers who set its direction.
A computer system is made of hardware and software, and a database stores records in tables.

sections.titre: Components, types and benefits of information systems
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Information system and its components
An **information system** collects, stores, processes and distributes data to produce information that people in an organisation use to operate and to decide. A computer-based information system has five components: **hardware** (computers, servers, tills, network equipment), **software** (operating system, database and application programs), **data** (the facts stored, such as customer and stock records), **people** (users, analysts, technicians and managers) and **procedures** (the rules and instructions for using the system, such as how to back up). Some books add the communication network as a sixth component.

Good information is **accurate, relevant, timely, complete and understandable**, and worth more than it costs.

### Types of information system
| System | Main users | Purpose | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| Transaction processing system (TPS) | operational staff | records and processes day-to-day transactions quickly and accurately | till sales, payroll, ticket booking |
| Management information system (MIS) | middle managers | summarises TPS data in regular reports so that performance can be monitored | monthly sales report by branch |
| Decision support system (DSS) | managers | analyses data with models and what-if questions to help with less routine decisions | testing how loan repayments change with the interest rate |
| Executive information system (EIS) | senior managers | gives a summarised view of internal and external data, with the option to look at the detail, for strategic decisions | dashboard of profit trends |
| Expert system | non-experts and professionals | a knowledge base of rules and an inference engine give advice like a human expert | help with diagnosing a fault |

### Benefits and costs for a business
A computer-based system processes data faster and more accurately, stores and retrieves records easily, supports better decisions through up-to-date summaries, serves customers faster and lets departments share the same data. The costs and risks are the purchase price, training, user resistance to change, dependence on power and equipment, and security risks.

variantes.nom: Match the system to the situation
variantes.quand_utiliser: When a short scenario asks which type of system is described.
variantes.contenu_markdown:
| Clue in the question | System |
|---|---|
| records each sale, booking or payment as it happens | TPS |
| regular summary reports for middle managers | MIS |
| what-if questions, models, a choice between options | DSS |
| strategic view for senior managers, dashboard | EIS |
| rules from an expert, advice to a non-expert | expert system |

Look for who uses the system and what decision it supports before choosing.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked for benefits or drawbacks of an information system to an organisation.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Write each point as the feature followed by its effect on the business. "Records are retrieved in seconds" is the feature; "so customers are served faster and the shop can handle more of them" is the effect that earns the mark. For disadvantages, give a cost and its consequence, for example staff training takes time and money before the benefits appear.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked to identify or describe the components of the system.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Name all five components, then give one example drawn from the organisation in the question. A list of devices such as a keyboard and a monitor is only the hardware and earns one mark at most. Remember the procedures: the written rules for entering data, backing up and handling faults.

sections.enonce_markdown:
A bakery has two branches. Its computer system records each sale. One day's sales are:

| No. | Branch | Product | Quantity | Unit price (FCFA) | Value (FCFA) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Branch 1 | Bread | 120 | 250 | 30 000 |
| 2 | Branch 1 | Cake | 4 | 3 000 | 12 000 |
| 3 | Branch 1 | Doughnut | 80 | 100 | 8 000 |
| 4 | Branch 2 | Bread | 90 | 250 | 22 500 |
| 5 | Branch 2 | Cake | 6 | 3 000 | 18 000 |
| 6 | Branch 2 | Doughnut | 50 | 100 | 5 000 |

(a) Identify the five components of the bakery's information system and give an example of each. [5 marks] (b) Name the type of system that records these sales, and the type that produces a report of the total value sold by each branch. Calculate the two totals. [4 marks] (c) The owner asks what would happen to the income from bread if its price rose from 250 FCFA to 300 FCFA and the quantity sold fell by 10 percent. Name the system that answers this and calculate the answer. [4 marks]

etapes.action: List the five components and apply each to the bakery.
etapes.justification: The question asks for the components in a named organisation, so each needs an example from it.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Hardware: the tills and the server. Software: the sales program and the database. Data: the sales records. People: the shop assistants and the manager. Procedures: the rules for closing the till and backing up each night.

etapes.action: Identify the system that records the sales.
etapes.justification: A system that captures each sale as it happens is a transaction processing system.

etapes.action: Total the values for each branch.
etapes.justification: A report that summarises transactions for a manager is the output of a management information system.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Branch 1: 50 000 FCFA. Branch 2: 45 500 FCFA. Report type: management information system (MIS).

etapes.action: Find the present income from bread.
etapes.justification: The what-if starts from the present value, which is the quantity multiplied by the price.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Bread sold: 120 + 90 = 210 loaves. Income: 210 x 250 = 52 500 FCFA.

etapes.action: Apply the changes in the what-if question.
etapes.justification: A quantity that falls by 10 percent becomes 90 percent of 210, and the new price is 300 FCFA.
etapes.resultat_markdown: New quantity = 189. New income = 189 x 300 = 56 700 FCFA, which is 4 200 FCFA more than before. The system that answers what-if questions is a decision support system (DSS).

sections.conclusion_markdown: **(a)** Hardware: tills and server. Software: the sales program and database. Data: the sales records. People: assistants, manager. Procedures: end-of-day closing and nightly backup. **(b)** The sales are recorded by a **transaction processing system**; the branch report is produced by a **management information system**. Branch 1 sold **50 000 FCFA** and Branch 2 sold **45 500 FCFA**. **(c)** A **decision support system** answers the question: the income from bread would rise from 52 500 FCFA to **56 700 FCFA** (an increase of 4 200 FCFA) if the assumption about sales holds. The result depends on the assumption, so the manager still makes the decision.

items.erreur_markdown: Answering "identify the components" with "computer, printer, keyboard and mouse".
items.pourquoi_faux: These are only items of hardware. A computer-based information system also needs software, data, people and procedures.
items.correction_markdown: Name hardware, software, data, people and procedures, with an example of each.

items.erreur_markdown: "Data and information are the same thing."
items.pourquoi_faux: Data are raw facts. Information is data that has been processed and organised so that it is useful.
items.correction_markdown: A list of sales figures is data; the total sold by each branch, shown in a report, is information.

items.erreur_markdown: "A transaction processing system produces strategic reports for senior managers."
items.pourquoi_faux: A TPS records day-to-day transactions. Summary reports belong to an MIS, and strategic overviews to an executive information system.
items.correction_markdown: TPS: operational records. MIS: summaries for middle managers. EIS: strategic view for senior managers.

items.erreur_markdown: "A decision support system makes the decision for the manager."
items.pourquoi_faux: A DSS supports a decision by analysing data and testing options. The manager judges the results and chooses.
items.correction_markdown: Say that the DSS helps the manager to compare alternatives and that the manager decides.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing "it is fast" as the advantage of an information system.
items.pourquoi_faux: The feature alone does not show a benefit to the business, so it earns little.
items.correction_markdown: "Records are retrieved in seconds, so customers are served faster and more customers can be handled."

items.enonce_markdown: Name the most suitable type of information system for each situation. (a) A bank records every deposit and withdrawal as it is made. (b) A company director looks at a summary dashboard of the whole company's profit over five years. (c) A manager changes the expected cost of fuel in a model to see the effect on the yearly budget. (d) A program asks a nurse questions and uses stored rules from specialist doctors to suggest the likely cause of an illness.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **Transaction processing system**: it records each transaction as it happens.

(b) **Executive information system**: a summarised strategic view for senior management.

(c) **Decision support system**: it tests what-if changes in a model.

(d) **Expert system**: a knowledge base of rules and an inference engine give advice to a non-expert.

items.enonce_markdown:
A bus agency in Douala records these bookings in its system.

| Booking | Route | Passengers | Fare per passenger (FCFA) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Douala-Yaounde | 10 | 3 500 |
| 2 | Douala-Bafoussam | 8 | 3 000 |
| 3 | Douala-Yaounde | 6 | 3 500 |
| 4 | Douala-Limbe | 12 | 1 500 |
| 5 | Douala-Bafoussam | 5 | 3 000 |

(a) Calculate the total income for each route. (b) Which route earned the most? (c) Name the type of system that produces a summary like the one in (a) from the booking records, and explain who uses it.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Income = passengers x fare, added for each route.

- Douala-Yaounde: $(10 + 6) \times 3\,500 = 16 \times 3\,500 = $ **56 000 FCFA**.
- Douala-Bafoussam: $(8 + 5) \times 3\,000 = 13 \times 3\,000 = $ **39 000 FCFA**.
- Douala-Limbe: $12 \times 1\,500 = $ **18 000 FCFA**.

(b) **Douala-Yaounde** earned the most. (The total for all routes is 113 000 FCFA.)

(c) A **management information system**. It summarises the transactions recorded by the transaction processing system into a report, which middle managers use to monitor performance and plan the number of buses on each route.

items.enonce_markdown: A microfinance office uses a computer model to compare loan offers. A customer borrows 600 000 FCFA for one year. Interest is charged once on the amount borrowed (flat rate), and the total is repaid in 12 equal monthly payments. (a) Calculate the monthly payment when the interest rate is 10 percent and when it is 12 percent. (b) Name the type of information system that lets an officer change the rate and see the new payment at once, and explain why it is suited to this task. (c) Give TWO disadvantages to the office of depending on such a system.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) At 10 percent: total repaid $= 600\,000 \times 1.10 = 660\,000$ FCFA, so each payment is $660\,000 \div 12 = $ **55 000 FCFA**. At 12 percent: total repaid $= 600\,000 \times 1.12 = 672\,000$ FCFA, so each payment is $672\,000 \div 12 = $ **56 000 FCFA**. The higher rate adds 1 000 FCFA to each payment.

(b) A **decision support system**. It holds a model of the loan calculation, so the officer can ask "what if the rate is 12 percent?" and see the new payment immediately, and compare several offers before the customer decides.

(c) Any two: cost of buying and maintaining the system; staff need training; the office cannot work if power or equipment fails; wrong data or a wrong model gives wrong advice; stored customer data must be protected.

items_markdown: A computer-based information system has five components: hardware, software, data, people and procedures.
Data are raw facts; information is processed data that is accurate, relevant, timely, complete and understandable.

TPS records day-to-day transactions; MIS summarises them for middle managers; DSS answers what-if questions; EIS gives senior managers a strategic view; an expert system gives advice from stored rules.
To match a system to a scenario, ask who uses it and what decision or task it supports.
Write each advantage as a feature followed by its effect on the business.
A DSS supports the manager's decision; it does not take it.
